title: Upper-case archive currency

change.goal: Show the currency code in upper case in the list, the page and the CSV export.
change.why: Some invoices show lower-case currency such as usd 10.00.
parts: readArchive upper-cases the archive's cur field when building an invoice

verdict: The change does its task. Service invoices are already validated as upper case by billing-client 2.3.0 (installed and locked), and the only source of lower case is the closed archive, which the schema says is always ^[a-z]{3}$. Fixing it at the single place where archive rows become invoices covers the list, page and CSV with one line.
target: readArchive normalises the archive's code to upper case; loadInvoices merges the service's and the archive's invoices; formatPrice and toCsv stay as they are. The change is already this.
recommendation: Accept as is. No findings; the ideas are optional.

requirements.text: Archive-origin invoices show their currency code in upper case in the invoice list
Service invoices (billing-client) keep working; no changes needed to them

ideas.title: Test through loadInvoices or the screens
ideas.text: A test that feeds a lower-case archive row through loadInvoices and formatPrice would pin the end-to-end requirement; costs a transport stub.

ideas.title: Refresh stale docs
ideas.text: The page describes billing-client 1.x (null and mixed-case currency); 2.x guarantees upper case and never null. Updating it prevents someone adding guards later; costs a doc edit outside this change.

units.name: fetchInvoices
jobs: fetches and validates service invoices, upper-case currency

blocks.does: Upper-cases the archive currency and documents why
Checks a lower-case archive row becomes an upper-case invoice

coverage: Read all of src, the schema, docs/billing.md, billing-client 2.3.0 source, types, changelog and lockfile, and the nested 1.4.0 copy under @acme/reports (not used by this code). Did not run tests. Archive rows are assumed to follow the schema; a missing cur would throw, but the schema requires it.
